column2: “Captain… We can talk later!” Old Tang said. “That thing’s coming!”
Outside Valhalla, light blazed as though the sun had risen early.

“Caesar! Thank God!” Fingel was beside himself. He lunged ahead of Nono and seized Caesar’s hand. “Find a way to stop him! At this point we can only count on your Student Council and Lionheart Society!”
With Fingel gripping his hand, Caesar had no idea what to say. He looked over Fingel’s shoulder at Nono. “Are you all right?”
“So far.” Nono picked up a fallen compact submachine gun. “I really don’t want to die on my birthday.”
Everyone had someone to catch up with except Lu Mingfei, who could only hop about anxiously. “Hurry! He’s coming!”
“Caesar! You handle things here!” Fingel grabbed Lu Mingfei. “Call in your Student Council elites and hold him off! You can do it.”
“All right,” Caesar said mildly.
Fingel and Lu Mingfei turned and ran, past the statue of Odin and straight toward the back door. Old Tang hesitated, then raced after them.
As Lu Mingfei reached the door, he glanced back at Nono. She and Caesar stood facing each other, and Caesar was gently patting her cheek.
“The leading man’s here. Your concern is no longer required!” Fingel twisted his head back around and shoved the PPK into his hand.
“Hey! Why give it to me?” Lu Mingfei asked.

“Who deserves this gun more than the S-rank who took out Caesar and Chu Zihang with two shots?” Fingel pulled the door firmly shut as he spoke. “Doesn’t everybody on the campus network call you Cassell’s Number One Sharpshooter?”
“Mingming, I have faith in you. You’re a genius with Marines.” Old Tang clapped him hard on the shoulder and gave him a thumbs-up.
“Could you two make any less sense?” Lu Mingfei gaped.
“Go after them.” Caesar smiled and took the gun from Nono’s hands.
“I stayed beside you when we played live-action Counter-Strike,” Nono said. “You know you can count on me.”

“That was only live-action Counter-Strike. You weren’t going to get hurt, so I didn’t have to worry. If you stay here, I’ll worry. You don’t have a Yanling. You’re different from me.” Caesar touched her forehead. “Go. I’ll hold him off for a little while, then retreat.”
Nono hesitated for a moment, then nodded.
“What’s my birthday present?” After a few steps she turned back to ask.
“A book.”
“A book?” Nono blinked. That was nothing like Caesar’s style. He liked extravagant presents.

“A book called Dragon Raja. I wrote it. It finished its run as a magazine serial and has just been collected and published. I was going to give you the first copy.” Caesar shrugged. “A secret present. I spent six months writing it without telling you.”
Nono nodded. “Then I’ll have this book you’re giving me before I go to sleep tomorrow night, right?”
“Of course. I don’t want to die on the first night I’ve ever celebrated my girlfriend’s birthday, either.”
Nono turned and ran for the back door. Watching her go, Caesar loaded AE rounds one by one into his Desert Eagles.

Mai had been leaning against the wall with her arms folded, watching the entire exchange without the slightest impulse to give them privacy. Head tilted, she listened calmly and openly, stretching her perfect figure as she did so: a dazzling third wheel.
“Your girlfriend seems pretty nice,” Mai said mildly.
“Yes. I’ve always liked the best,” Caesar said coldly.
“Oh, well. Chips Girl always leaves me with nowhere to run!” Mai began changing the magazine in her Glock.
“A thirty-three-round extended magazine?” Caesar glanced at her. “You aren’t running? You look ready to fight to the death.”

“Don’t get the wrong idea. I’m not looking to share your hardships.” Mai shrugged, lifting her elegantly shaped chin toward the unconscious people scattered over the floor. “It’s for these guys. I can’t move them right now, and if that dragon gets in here, I can’t be sure they’ll survive.”
“That kind of self-sacrifice doesn’t sound like you.”
“As captain, I simply can’t stand being a coward.”
Facing each other, Caesar and Mai finished loading and racked their slides at the same instant. Just then, Mai’s phone rang.
“Chips, if I were going to die, what would your last words to me be?” Mai asked.
“Nonmetals can hurt him!” the woman said.
“What?”

“The King of Bronze and Fire has absolute authority over flame and metal within his domain. That’s why metal bullets can’t injure him. Any bullet that approaches is instantly melted and slowed to a stop,” the woman said. “But he can’t control nonmetals. So unless his domain collapses, Frigga rounds are far more effective against him than live ammunition.”
“The anesthetic in Frigga rounds will work on him?”

“No. It won’t. At that temperature, the anesthetic instantly vaporizes and decomposes. It stops working before it can enter his bloodstream! But the kinetic energy of a Frigga round still affects him. In other words, you can’t shoot him dead, but you can drive him back.”

“Chips, I can still count on you for backup. The only problem is…” Mai suddenly raised her voice and swore. “You’re so goddamn slow I have to reload my magazine again! I just put thirty-three ordinary rounds into my Glock!”
She closed her phone and exchanged a look with Caesar. Both began changing ammunition at once. They could already hear footsteps approaching Valhalla.

The instant that slender, blindingly bright figure appeared at Valhalla’s entrance, Caesar and Mai sprang up together, their Glocks and Desert Eagles pouring bullets into it as fast as they could fire.

The Frigga rounds worked. The figure twisted under the barrage, retreating step by step. Each round burst into blood-red mist as it approached him, yet the mist pushed him backward. Caesar and Mai took turns changing magazines and firing, forcing him bodily out of Valhalla. The brutal recoil of their continuous gunfire had almost numbed their wrists, but they gritted their teeth and kept shooting. Every measure of force exerted on their wrists exerted an equal force on that dragon. They could only advance; there was no retreat. They must never let him cross the threshold behind them.

Listening to the fighting in Valhalla, Schneider’s eyes suddenly lit up. He shouted into the microphone, “Yes… yes! Frigga rounds can drive him back! Everyone, switch to Frigga rounds! Keep firing. Don’t give him a chance to use Yanling!”
The students hidden in the darkness rose one after another. A storm of bullets struck the figure being pushed out of Valhalla, enveloping him entirely in blood-red mist.
“Hey, did we come here to swim?” Lu Mingfei asked. “I thought we came for shelter.”

“Of course we came for shelter. Water is the greatest enemy of fire-type Yanling.” Fingel was very serious. “If you’d studied Yanling, you’d understand. Its symbol is a pentagram. Earth, water, wind, fire, and spirit—the five elements keep each other in check. Fire-type Yanling can penetrate many barriers, but it has difficulty crossing a body of water. So if he’s finding you through some sort of fire-type Yanling, this is the safest place. It’s the largest body of water at Cassell College.”
“Senior, you’re treading water in the deep end in nothing but your underwear while talking like an academic. I have trouble understanding what that feels like,” Lu Mingfei said.
“Keep treading. Hold that PPK above the surface. Don’t get it wet. If the guy really does come after us, shoot him.”
“But just now you said that if he came after us, we should hold our breath and hide underwater.”
“Good point. I should get you a plastic bag.”
In Cassell College’s enormous indoor pool, Fingel, Lu Mingfei, and Old Tang were treading water furiously. Lu Mingfei had to be grateful he had some foundation in swimming.

Fingel’s argument did seem to make sense. They had been treading water here for fifteen minutes, and the dragon still hadn’t come after them. Before, wherever they sought shelter, he had tracked them down in less than five minutes, like a dog following their scent.
“Oh, introductions. This is my friend, Old Tang,” Lu Mingfei said. “And this is my senior, Fingel.”
“Hello.” Two people whose allegiances should never have aligned shook hands.
“That girl was Nono, the girlfriend of our college’s Student Council boss. She’s my senior,” Lu Mingfei said. “Don’t get the wrong idea, Old Tang.”
He was gradually relaxing, beginning to feel they could chat to pass the time. Waiting around like this was unsettling too.

“I understand. Getting involved with the boss’s woman gets you three stabs and six holes. Something you can do but can’t talk about. I grew up in America, but I’m still Chinese. I understand Chinese culture,” Old Tang said. “My only regret right now is that the boss’s woman didn’t come tread water with us…”
“Just imagining the scene gives me a nosebleed,” Fingel said.
“So, Old Tang, how did you end up here?” Lu Mingfei asked.

“I told you I’m a bounty hunter, right? There’s a website for our line of work that specializes in slightly supernatural cases. New jobs are posted regularly. Employers never show their faces. People with sufficient rank can view the details and decide whether to apply. If the employer likes your résumé, you get a letter. Once the job’s done, the fee goes straight into your account.”
“I had no idea your line of work was so cool,” Lu Mingfei said.

“I’m not really good at anything else.” Old Tang seemed a little shy. “I just seem to have a natural resistance to supernatural things. Ancient tombs affect other people, for example, but not me. Some curses with very reliable reputations in the business don’t work on me either. So my rank’s pretty high. I can take big jobs like this one, worth five million dollars.”
“Five million?” Fingel’s eyes widened.

“But I didn’t expect it to be this dangerous. Originally they only said to find something at this college. And then… If I’d known, I wouldn’t have come. I’d still be asleep in New York. Money’s a little tight, but I could afford to take you around America on Greyhounds,” Old Tang said. “You’re a loyal friend, brother. I won’t forget it.”
“I want to tour America on Greyhounds too…” Fingel said.
Old Tang’s expression suddenly changed. “I don’t know why… but I feel like… he’s coming after us.”
“No, is he?” Lu Mingfei pricked up his sensitive rabbit ears. “I can’t hear anything. Not a sound…”

He stopped abruptly, his face turning deathly pale too. In the sports hall, which should have been empty, a single set of footsteps echoed closer and closer, until it seemed only a wall separated them. With it came a call that made his scalp crawl:
“Brother… Brother…”
“The ghost… the ghost followed us!” Lu Mingfei shuddered violently several times. “Now what?”

Fingel looked grim too. He handed each of them a plastic bag. “Don’t panic. His footsteps are circling the pool. That means he knows we’re nearby, but the water keeps him from pinpointing us. It’s no surprise he guessed we were here. The sports hall is directly behind Valhalla. Let’s not scare ourselves. If we show ourselves now, he’ll spot us. Each of us can take a bag of air underwater, take a few breaths when we can’t hold out anymore, and last a few minutes. Once we’re completely surrounded by water, fire-type Yanling won’t be able to find us at all. When he loses our trail, he’ll leave. He doesn’t seem quite right in the head. Probably a mentally disturbed dragon.”
“He really is a dragon? Why would a dragon have a human form?” Lu Mingfei asked.

“Dragons come in nine kinds. That pretty girl fighting Caesar might be a dragon too, for all you know. One final warning: don’t get nervous. That’ll only give you away. The water will form a water-sealed boundary that hides every trace of you. The Yangtze is a perfect water-sealed boundary, or that ancient bronze city wouldn’t have stayed hidden so long. Trust me. I used to be A-rank.” With that, Fingel pressed their heads beneath the water.

Lu Mingfei held his breath and submerged his face, not daring to open his eyes. He swam well; he simply disliked opening his eyes underwater, because everything turned pale blue and he felt as though he were alone on another planet. The water wasn’t heated at night, and the cold made him shiver a little.

He had no idea how much time passed. Nothing happened, but the pool gradually grew warmer, as though the heating system had come on. At this temperature, Lu Mingfei thought, he could stay underwater as long as he liked, provided air wasn’t a problem. But the good times didn’t last. Soon it grew absurdly hot. Had Fingel set the wrong temperature on the way in? The pool was practically bathwater now.
A little longer, and it was almost scalding.

Lu Mingfei grew restless. The air in his plastic bag was nearly gone, and the heat of the pool was unbearable. Perhaps the dragon had wandered elsewhere by now, and he could lift his head for a look. He reached out to tap Fingel and Old Tang, but found nothing. He swept both hands from side to side without touching anyone.

Frightened, he cautiously rose to the surface and looked around. White steam filled his vision. The pool must have reached forty degrees Celsius. Any hotter and it really would be a hot spring. He couldn’t see Fingel or Old Tang. Perhaps they had found the heat unbearable too and climbed out.
“Surely Old Tang and Fingel haven’t… both been eaten?” he thought. They did look tastier than he did, but there was no reason the dragon should have no interest whatsoever in his skinny bones.

He climbed out using the ladder. In that short time, the water had grown hotter still, steaming like a boiling pot of soup. The swimming hall had become a giant sauna. He couldn’t even see where the doors were.
Not daring to call out, he felt his way through the steam along the edge of the pool. If he could find even one of them, Fingel or Old Tang, he wouldn’t feel so frightened.
He heard splashing. A figure swam to the edge and began climbing out.
“Who can stand water that hot?” Relieved, Lu Mingfei hurried toward the pool in little steps, hitching up his soaked underwear.

He froze. The face he saw in the white vapor belonged to neither Fingel nor Old Tang. It was a delicate-featured boy, climbing the ladder out of the water. He looked a little younger than Lu Mingfei, only sixteen or seventeen, with a small face, faint eyebrows, and eyes of an even, pure black. Yet his gaze was utterly vacant. His naked body was deathly pale and so thin that every rib stood out.
He stared blankly at Lu Mingfei for a few seconds.
“I’m not looking for you. I’m looking for my brother. Have you seen him?” the boy asked, his voice distant and drifting.
“No.” Lu Mingfei shook his head, wondering who his brother was.
“I’ll go look for him, then. Goodbye.” The boy brushed past Lu Mingfei, his body searingly hot, its heat washing against Lu Mingfei’s face.
Lu Mingfei turned and watched the boy slowly disappear into the white vapor.
“Brother… Brother…” the boy called, his voice growing fainter.

That voice sounded familiar… Lu Mingfei suddenly felt as though each goose bump on his body were about to leap off his skin. He remembered where he had heard it. The dragon’s calls had sounded exactly like this. Repeated echoes in the corridors had merely made them seem more elusive, like a wailing ghost.
Had he just had a conversation with a dragon?

He dared not think any further. Enormous fear threatened to swallow him whole. Snatching his clothes from beside the pool, he pulled them on as he ran. There was no white vapor in the corridor. He raced all the way to the emergency exit at the rear, pushed the door open, and took a deep breath of fresh air before feeling a little safer.
But he froze again. An old man stood outside, hands in his trouser pockets, neatly groomed white hair above a black suit, a bright red rose tucked into his breast pocket.
Judging by his face, he must have been very, very old. Judging by the way he stood, he was a young man through and through.
“Lu Mingfei. I’ve been looking for you.” The old man smiled.
“Principal… Anjou!” Lu Mingfei’s eyes went wide.
The principal led Lu Mingfei upstairs. An iron staircase on the side of the chapel zigzagged up the building, which was now almost a ruin.

Outside the attic beneath the bell was a balcony with an extraordinarily wide view. The attic itself was a mess. An old cowboy sat on the sofa drinking beer. How the fellow had remained so unshakably calm while two lunatics below blasted each other with Sovereign Flame was anybody’s guess.
“Hey, Anjou. Is this our new S-rank?” The old cowboy raised a hand to Lu Mingfei. “Hello, young man.”
Lu Mingfei returned the greeting woodenly.

The principal led him to the balcony, opened a case in front of him, and assembled a large-caliber sniper rifle, which he handed to Lu Mingfei. Lu Mingfei accepted it in silence. Neither said a word throughout. The principal then produced a sealed cylindrical quartz-glass tube and showed him what was inside: a long, slender cartridge with a dark red bullet, like a roughly polished red crystal, a bloodlike luster flowing and shifting within.
“The fifth element. The Philosopher’s Stone,” the principal said. “An alchemical bullet. Its tip is made of pure spirit. Only this can kill a Dragon King. Make the shot count. These are very rare.”
He loaded the cartridge, chambered it with a click, and patted Lu Mingfei’s shoulder.
“Principal… What is this for?” Lu Mingfei finally managed his first words.

The principal pointed across the campus. Squads were converging on Valhalla. Above the rooster on its roof stood a blindingly bright figure: the dragon, calling hoarsely across the entire campus. Students shot Frigga rounds at him as they ran, enveloping him entirely in blood-red mist. Waving his arms to shield his face, he kept calling.
“Brother!”
He really was like a vengeful ghost, enough to send a chill through anyone.

“That is the Dragon King. I’ll break through his defenses for you. In a moment you’ll see an eye turning—his third dragon eye. That is his weak point. Aim at his forehead and shoot him with this bullet,” the principal said. “Can you do it?”

Lu Mingfei looked at the sniper rifle in his hands. It was a top-of-the-line weapon with an infrared laser sight. For anyone with a little shooting experience, hitting the target would be nothing remarkable. Missing would be the surprise. The range wasn’t particularly long, either.
“But why me?” He was bewildered.

“Because you were chosen. Believe in your bloodline. You’re the one and only S-rank! Only you can be immune to my Yanling: Eternity.” From an inner pocket of his suit, the principal drew a folding knife. It was large and antiquated, with an exquisite brass-inlaid wooden handle. Twisting patterns covered the slightly curved blade, an extremely rare piece of patterned steel. In ancient times, such precious meteoric iron had been reserved for the swords of heroes.
The principal noticed Lu Mingfei looking at his knife. “This is my weapon. My friend Meinhard Cassell made it for me from the broken tip of his own blade. Very useful.”
He turned and headed downstairs. “Watch my performance in a moment. The rest is up to you, Lu Mingfei.”

Old Tang ran across the lawn, desperate to leave this goddamned place. He felt a little guilty. For some reason, he had been terrified back there. Those footsteps had seemed to sound inside his mind. He had felt there was no way hiding underwater would save him, and had been unable to stop himself from quietly climbing out and slipping away.
He felt he had let Lu Mingfei down, but that fear had been truly unbearable.
“Stop! Stop!” Fingel chased him from far behind. “You can’t escape him by running like that! He…”

Fingel turned toward the roof of Valhalla and was struck speechless with terror. The dragon had evidently detected their location. Deafening cracks came from every bone in his body, the skin of his back split, and a pair of membranous wings that had lain folded against it suddenly spread wide, streaming blood.
With that advantage in the air, catching them would be far too easy.

The principal appeared on the lawn. He crouched like a leopard, gathering all his strength into his legs with a young man’s poise. Chanted Draconic swept across the campus. High above, the dragon lowered his head to look at the old man.
Everyone could feel the old man’s spirit expanding in an instant through the darkness.
Yanling: Eternity.

Lu Mingfei suddenly noticed something impossible. Time throughout the campus seemed to slow. The running students, the dragon spreading his membranous wings, even the leaves swaying in the wind and the rolling flames—all slowed down. Through the scope, the dragon’s eyes opened and closed slowly. Only he and the principal had not slowed. The principal moved like a leopard, racing across the lawn and springing up the fire escape to Valhalla’s roof. Even a Marine or a martial arts master from ancient China could have done no better.
He approached the dragon with nothing but that folding knife in his hand.
“Lu Mingfei!” The principal’s voice exploded through the air.

Lu Mingfei had no choice but to concentrate entirely on the scope. He followed the principal’s advance through it; the principal would show him his target. At that moment, the dragon-slaying warriors of every age seemed to live again in this old man. Before the age of science, this was how they had fought, relying on the advantages of their bloodlines, on courage and sacrifice, to transcend human limitations.

Blazing fire radiated from the dragon, but many times more slowly than before, like a film in slow motion. The principal slipped through the gaps in the flames and, the instant he came within reach, swung his folding knife and spun.
Both of the dragon’s arms fell. He had not even reacted, merely staring straight ahead, apparently still unaware that the principal had flashed behind him.
The center of his forehead split open. The principal had slashed it vertically with his knife. A reddish-gold eye burst from the wound and slowly turned.

The third dragon eye. His weak point. This was the perfect opportunity the principal had created for him. Suddenly Lu Mingfei understood. There had not been a single wasted movement. Severing the arms meant the dragon could no longer shield himself.
Through his scope, he saw the dragon’s face clearly.

His hands trembled slightly. It really was the face of the child he had seen at the pool. After evaporating a great quantity of water there, the dragon had revealed his true appearance. No matter how he looked at him, he was only a lost child… “I’m not looking for you,” the child had said, as though they had known each other before.
At the very last instant, he shifted his aim slightly aside and pulled the trigger.

The bullet fashioned from the Philosopher’s Stone left the muzzle slowly enough for him to see with his naked eyes. Now nothing could be changed. He straightened up, lowered the rifle, and watched it drift through the air.
It was a very strange feeling.
A hit! Scalding blood burst from the dragon eye. The dragon clutched his forehead and roared hoarsely.
“What kept you from making up your mind, Lu Mingfei?” The principal turned toward the high reaches of the chapel.
The dragon beat his membranous wings, flew from Valhalla’s roof, and swooped toward the fleeing Old Tang. Seeing the shadow sweep down over him, Old Tang fell backward in terror.
“Switch to live ammunition!” The principal’s voice sounded over every student’s communications channel.

They had no time to think, and no need to. The principal was this campus’s absolute leader. Hundreds of guns were reloaded with live ammunition and aimed at the dragon gliding through the night. They had not even noticed Old Tang in the darkness.
The dragon landed opposite Old Tang. Behind him, hundreds of rounds slid into chambers, and firing pins struck primers.
He realized what was about to happen. Suddenly he spread his wings like an enormous barrier, enclosing Old Tang within them.

Gunfire set the entire dark campus ablaze. Thousands of live rounds struck the dragon’s body. He had lost the Yanling power that commanded metal, and could only block them with his back and wings. The students changed magazines over and over until they had emptied every one. They dared not stop. Throughout that savage barrage, the dragon stood rooted in place. He did not fall.
What unearthly vitality!
The last bullet left its barrel. Acrid gunsmoke filled the campus. Everyone stared at the figure standing amid the smoke, wings spread like a god.

Old Tang stared too, watching his face. The dragon was as ruined as a rotting corpse nailed to a cross, riddled with countless holes that let the light through. However resilient his dragon bones, without the power of Yanling they were only a good material. Every bone and joint in his spread wings had been pulverized. Fragments were falling away.
Light no longer flowed over him. He had turned a bleak gray-white. He smiled wearily at Old Tang. “Brother…”
“No… Don’t come after me! I don’t know you!” Old Tang screamed and turned to run. Behind him, the dragon’s body collapsed.
Old Tang raced along the winding mountain road. He did not know what he was fleeing; he simply wanted to escape. The dragon was already dead, yet something still seemed to be pursuing him.
“Brother, there are so many people outside.”
“We’re going to die, Constantine. But don’t be afraid.”
“I’m not afraid. With you here, Brother, I’m not afraid… But why… won’t you eat me? If you eat me, you can break out of any prison.”
“You would make very good food. But then I would be so lonely. For thousands of years, you’ve been the only one with me.”
“But death is so sad. Forever and ever, blacker than black… Like groping through the night, reaching out your hands, but never touching anything…”

“The fate of the forsaken is to cross the wilderness, raise their battle banners once more, and return to their homeland. Death is nothing to fear. It is only a long sleep. Until I can devour this world, I would rather sleep in peace than wander alone. We will wake again.”
“Brother… If one day we raise the war banner and can devour the world, will you eat me?”
“Yes. Then you and I will rule the world together!”
He remembered. What was pursuing him was memory.
He stopped dead, tearing desperately at his hair, and cried soundlessly into the pitch-black sky.
“Little brother!”
He remembered. He remembered everything.
So all these two thousand years, asleep or awake, you only wanted to find me. But when you found me, I had already forgotten what you looked like.
By the time I remembered your face, you were dead.
Fierce flames rose around his body into the night. High overhead, the fire burst open, as though a pair of wings had spread within it.

“The dragonbone cross. The Dragon King Norton has finally revealed his true self, the face of wrath.” In the chapel bell tower, Principal Anjou drained his martini. “Listen to his cry. How many years of loneliness and pain saturate it? It… no, he has fully returned to life, with a martyr’s soul.”

“Anjou, you knew all along that each throne of the Four Monarchs is occupied by twins. With your abilities, could you really have failed to notice that the ‘cargo’ delivered here was the older brother who escaped the sealed brass jar eighty years ago and later fell in the Lop Nur Desert? You could easily have erased him, but you didn’t. What exactly are you trying to do?” the old cowboy asked.
“I’ve grown tired,” the principal said quietly.
“Of what? Your life as a dragon slayer, or yourself?”

“Both, I suppose. I’ve lived for over a hundred years. Thanks to the gift of dragon blood, I’m not dead yet. Over those hundred years, all my friends have died. You’re the only old fellow left. We’re two strange old flowers at Cassell College that should have withered long ago, yet here we stand, drinking martinis, with the hot blood of resurrected Dragon Kings splashing onto our hands.” The principal looked at his hands.

“Because the younger generation can’t shoulder the responsibility of protecting this world yet. The leader of a new generation, the one we’ve always hoped for, still hasn’t arrived.” The old cowboy was silent for a moment. “Lu Mingfei. You think highly of that boy? Does he have a chance?”

“I don’t know yet. Over nearly a century, there have been more than a few gifted young people like him. But rising stars keep falling, while we two old men still haven’t died,” the principal said. “I can’t wait any longer, Leonardo. I can’t wait any longer. I’ll use the time I have left to finish what I must, to settle this war between humans and dragons once and for all.”
“You want to destroy the dragons… instead of continually preventing their awakening?”
“Yes. I want to kill the Four Monarchs!”

The old cowboy was silent for a while. “According to Norse mythology, fate begins with Urd, is measured out by Verdandi, and must finally be cut by Skuld’s scissors. At the end of human history, the Black King Nidhogg will return. He is despair, and he is hell. With wings hung with human bones, he will blot out the sky. He is Skuld’s scissors. On the day of his vengeance, even if you are Odin, when you leave your palace bearing your undefeated spear, the road beneath your feet will lead only to a place of no return. Isn’t this the prophecy we’ve believed for over a hundred years? We can only delay that day, never change its ending. Fate is called fate precisely because it cannot be changed.” He paused. “And now you intend to change it?”
The principal nodded. “To kill the Dragon Kings, we must give them no way out. Force them to stake their almost eternal lives on a fight to the finish with humanity.”
“No way out?”
“Yes. I’m going to give them no way out,” the principal said softly. “For an immortal life, as long as it goes on living, there is always hope. What would leave it no way out?”
“When its closest kin are killed, when it no longer wants to live, there will be no way out.” The old cowboy sighed.
“Those dragonbone crosses burning in the sky will be their gravestones!”
The principal made a call. “Caesar Gattuso. Anjou here. I’d like to invite you to my office for tea.”
Morning sunlight streamed into Room 303. Lu Mingfei sat blankly at his desk, fingers clattering over his laptop keyboard.
He opened the campus news homepage. The lead story read: “Caesar, Could You Be Any More of a Casanova?”

“Student Council president Caesar Gattuso spent tens of thousands of dollars on fireworks to celebrate his girlfriend Chen Motong’s birthday… Last night, custom fireworks were set off in the valley, displaying the words ‘NoNo, Happy Birthday!’ Yesterday happened to be the twentieth birthday of Chen Motong, the Red-haired Witch. And amid those dazzling fireworks, Caesar fought the strangers who had invaded campus with a pistol in each hand at Valhalla, shooting at the Dragon King Norton. He’s done so many spectacular things that we’ve almost gone numb, but we on the campus news team still have to say: Caesar, you’ve outdone yourself as a Casanova again. So much so that we’d be embarrassed not to make you the headline!”

The accompanying picture showed enormous fireworks bursting and falling against the black sky like burning gold dust. Their light illuminated a waterfall gleaming silver as it plunged from the mountaintop.
Head hanging, Lu Mingfei kept typing.

No one would ever believe something this spectacular had anything to do with him anyway. Wasn’t it the same trick Yang Guo used to charm Guo Xiang in The Return of the Condor Heroes? Yang Guo had been so cool: the Condor Hero, wandering the world with a dark-iron greatsword on his shoulder and a condor taller than a man at his side. How hard could it be for him to charm little Guo Xiang, who hadn’t even finished puberty?
What claim did Lu Mingfei have to a Casanova’s exploits like those?

Even if he could somehow pass for Yang Guo, Caesar and Nono would be the married couple Guo Jing and Huang Rong. He could give Huang Rong fireworks, and the whole world would think Hero Guo had sent them… Perfectly natural, really.

“By the way, yesterday we ate at Caesar’s expense, and you received flirtatious glances from Kiran, president of the Freshman Association, and encouragement from Chu Zihang. Any thoughts about which gang… sorry, club you’re going to join?” Fingel asked from the top bunk.
“I’ve decided. I’m joining the Student Council’s Clubs Department! I’m writing Caesar a letter right now.” Lu Mingfei didn’t look up.

Fingel stared for several seconds. “Good God! Have you grown a brain? Do you have the slightest understanding of political struggle? You’re after his girlfriend, and now you’re joining his club? Caesar will have no shortage of ways to make your life miserable.”

“I just think having my senior look out for me would be pretty nice.” Lu Mingfei shrugged. “If you were the great and glorious Caesar, would you bother giving someone like me a hard time?” He clicked Send. “There! Done! My pledge to join the mountain bandits is on its way!”
Someone knocked on the dorm room door.
Fingel went to open it. Pacino, a Student Council officer in an immaculate suit, stood outside. He handed an envelope to Lu Mingfei, who had come over.
“Your Student Council ID card. Welcome aboard.” Pacino held out his hand. “From now on, we’re friends.”
“What… what kind of efficiency is this?” Lu Mingfei’s face twitched. All he could do was offer his hand. “I… I only just sent my pledge… I mean, my email.”

“Chen Motong, head of the Clubs Department, said she was certain you would choose the Student Council. Her exact words were, ‘This kid can’t escape my clutches.’ So your card was printed in advance. We’ve been waiting downstairs since early this morning. Just now Chen Motong called to confirm your application email had arrived, and we came straight up.” Pacino spoke with impeccable politeness, gripping Lu Mingfei’s hand so firmly that he felt he had just joined the Communist Party and was receiving a warm welcome from the organization.
“As a new member of the Student Council, Caesar invites you to a meeting at Amber Hall,” Pacino said.
“Nani? What? Is this some kind of mistake?” Lu Mingfei’s eyes went round.

“No mistake. You’ve been assigned to Operation Bronze. After last night’s battle, the principal and I had a meeting. Last night’s incident was the awakening of a first-generation dragon. Dragon awakenings will accelerate. In February 2010, we’ll carry out a dragon-slaying mission on the Yangtze, code name Bronze. Normally this is the Executive Department’s work, but its personnel are scattered around the world, and some must remain to guard the college. We’re short of people, so Professor Manstein will lead this operation, and the Student Council will send some trainees. I recommended you.” Caesar was very direct.

“Hey, hey! Caesar, my man, isn’t dragon slaying… a specialized technical job? I’ve only been here a few weeks… and you’re already talking about slaying dragons… Speaking of dragons, I haven’t even handed in my Alchemical Chemistry paper yet!”
Lu Mingfei had not expected his visit to Amber Hall to be a prebattle mobilization briefing.

“Starting tomorrow, you can stop attending classes and prepare for intensive training.” Caesar studied an enormous chart on the workbench beside him without turning around. “You cannot refuse. Everyone here today is taking part in Operation Bronze. Only two first-years were selected, and you are one of them. Consider it an honor.”
“Honor, my ass! Has your sense of honor packed your brain so tight it’s ready to burst?” Lu Mingfei thought.

“You could at least ask first, couldn’t you? In China, even when a teacher has already decided to make me take the fall, he still says, ‘Student Lu Mingfei, the organization has an honorable and arduous assignment for you. Are you willing to accept?’”
“Very well.” Caesar looked up. “Student Lu Mingfei, the organization has an honorable and arduous assignment for you. Are you willing to accept?”
“No!” Lu Mingfei said loudly.
“I knew you would say that. That’s why I told you that you cannot refuse,” Caesar said mildly.
Lu Mingfei was speechless.
“Accept it. The other first-year has already accepted. Could you stop wasting time?”
“What lunatic would accept? You’re lying to me, aren’t you? Do you think I’m stupid?” Lu Mingfei said.
“I did, in fact, accept calmly.” Someone stepped out from the side.

There was really no need for her to say “calmly.” Her entirely uninflected voice already made it clear she was calm. Extremely calm. As calm as if someone had told her they were going to the bathroom.

Zero stood quietly beside Lu Mingfei in her school uniform. It was the first time he had seen her wearing it. In terms of size, that custom-made uniform could probably only be classed as children’s wear. In it, she looked like a well-behaved princess of the tsars.
“Hey! What are you doing here?” Lu Mingfei stared.
“I’m a member of the Student Council too. Why shouldn’t I be here?” Zero asked.
“Doesn’t that icy look of yours practically announce, ‘I don’t give anyone the time of day’? Why would you join club activities?”
“No. I’m very enthusiastic about club activities. I like being with everyone,” Zero said.

“How is anyone supposed to see ‘enthusiasm’ on a face that’s definitely below freezing?” Lu Mingfei was losing his mind. “Hey, have you thought this through? People die on these missions! Die! Look at you. Eighteen at most, fourteen if we go by your height… You have your whole life ahead of you. I bet you don’t even have a boyfriend yet. Wouldn’t dying now be a terrible waste?”
Zero gave him an icy glance. “Shut up!”
“I… I only joined today…” Lu Mingfei stammered. “I only handed in my application this morning… Doesn’t the organization need to vet me first?”

“That’s all right. Haven’t you already received the Student Council card we prepared for you? You are a full member,” Caesar said. “Also, the principal asked me to tell you all that if you complete this mission, he’ll give you perfect marks in every subject this semester. That means a 4.0 GPA for your first semester.”
Everyone applauded. Lu Mingfei alone felt as though the end had come.
“But I didn’t come here for a 4.0 GPA, okay?” he muttered.
“Then, Lu Mingfei, why did you come here?” Caesar turned, looking down at him with menace in his ice-blue eyes.
Lu Mingfei froze.

“Once you discovered that every student at this college has dragon blood, yet our goal is to slay dragons, and that everyone who comes here must take risks—risks of life and death—why didn’t you leave? All it takes is filling out the withdrawal paperwork. The Executive Department has plenty of ways to erase your memories. When you return to China, they’ll even fabricate your experiences in America for you. You can go back to your old life.” Caesar looked straight into his eyes. “Someone has told you all this, haven’t they?”
“Yes.” Lu Mingfei lowered his head and scratched his ear.
“Then why didn’t you choose to withdraw?” Caesar asked.
A dozen or so people stood in the room. No one spoke. It was so quiet that every breath could be heard. As Caesar asked, he looked around, as though questioning everyone, not only Lu Mingfei.
At that moment, Caesar looked more like a leader than ever.
“Well, there are… personal reasons.” After a long silence, Lu Mingfei mumbled his answer.

He looked at the black card in his hand. There were only two lines on it. The first, stamped in silver, read “Union of Dragonese,” the Dragonblood Union. The second, in smaller type, read “Ricardo M. Lu.”
His Student Council membership card. Ricardo M. Lu, member of the Clubs Department.
“I really don’t know how I got to this point,” he told himself.
Cold laughter sounded behind him. Lu Mingfei shuddered. He recognized that laugh: Lu Mingze’s. He spun around, trying to pick the mysterious boy out of the crowd.
He found no one. In the direction of the laughter, Nono was hiding behind a burly Student Council officer, trying to pin up Zero’s hair…
“What are you doing?” Following Lu Mingfei’s gaze, Caesar saw what Nono was up to and frowned.
“Oh.” Nono let go of Zero’s hair and shrugged indifferently.

“In any case, you know everything now. You can still choose to withdraw. If you forgo that option, you’ll take part in the mission. The withdrawal procedures are very straightforward too.” Caesar looked at Lu Mingfei. “I’d be happy with that, because I only work with the best. S-rank or not, if you’re a cowardly piece of trash, I don’t want to see you.”

“Attention, everyone. We begin two months of intensive training. After that, we fly to China to launch our first decisive battle against the dragons. Internal code name: Bronze!” Caesar raised his hand.

Everyone raised a hand with him, but no one spoke. It was a silent oath. Lu Mingfei followed suit dejectedly, feeling he had been taken hostage by these lunatics’ grand ideals and unwavering convictions.
Slaying dragons. Was that really something he could do? In truth, his reason for not withdrawing… had nothing whatsoever to do with ideals, loneliness, ambition, or any of that.
It was just one tiny, tiny little reason.
“Hey, don’t worry.” Nono stood beside him and nudged him with an elbow. “Relax. You’re my little follower, not Caesar’s. I’ll look out for you!”
“You?” Lu Mingfei glanced at her. You don’t even know what your own Yanling is, he thought, and you’re going to look out for me?

Looking at himself in the mirror, Lu Mingfei had no idea what material this damned close-fitting combat suit was made of. It clung to him like a tough second skin, reminding him of the underwear in TV commercials that promised to burn fat, slim your legs, and shrink your waist.
“You’ve been staring at yourself like that for fifteen minutes.” Fingel poked his head down from the top bunk.
Lu Mingfei sighed. “I’m just wondering whether I look more like Jiuyue, the master thief from Star-Stealing September, or Rei Ayanami from EVA.”

“Hey, other people are ecstatic when they get an Executive Department combat uniform. They turn this way and that in front of the mirror too, but they’re admiring the insignia on their epaulettes and their belts, trying out a few cool quick-draw poses. You’re imagining your graceful anime-girl curves?” Fingel said. “Wake up, wake up, wake up! Is there anything in your life besides fantasies about anime characters?”
“Games too.”
“Still a geek…” Fingel shook his head.
“So, my loser senior, you’ve repeated four years. Why are you still at Cassell College?” Lu Mingfei sat on the edge of his bed, looking through the open window at a sky full of stars.

“As a loser senior, I’ve devoted myself to the study of dragon genetics and bloodlines. I can’t do anything else… Do you think I could make a living if I left?” From some corner of his filthy blanket, Fingel produced a waffle, stuffed it into his mouth, and began chewing noisily.
“But you might die,” Lu Mingfei said, hanging his head.
“Don’t worry. I’ve figured it out. I’ll give you remote support!” Fingel reached down and patted his head.
“Remote support?”
“I’ll stay online the whole time. You just need to bring something that can connect to the internet. With your abilities and my intelligence, what problem couldn’t we solve?”

“That sounds like, ‘Look at our plate of potatoes stewed with cucumbers! What emperor would dare say it isn’t delicious?’” The faint hope that had just arisen in Lu Mingfei’s heart collapsed again. “This time… they’re saving money.”
“How?” Fingel blinked.
“My medical insurance. The maximum coverage is flying my remains back to China… Now I’m about to fly myself to China and die there. Quite a saving, isn’t it?”

“Like a pig walking itself onto the slaughter line?” Fingel said in a low voice. “Your tragic mood is getting to me too… But seriously, you have to believe I know a great deal of theory. And I’m absolutely the number one guy on Cassell College’s network. To tell you the truth, with my skills I can still access the school network with A-rank clearance. It just involves a little risk.”
After a silence, Lu Mingfei said, “Fingel, sometimes I think you’re pretty far out to lunch…”
“Come on, don’t put it like that…” Fingel interrupted.
“But sometimes I think you really do treat me pretty well.” Lu Mingfei looked up at Fingel’s face, half hidden by tangled hair. “Do you spend so much time bothering with me because you’re too bored?”

“Come on, don’t put it like that…” Fingel was silent for a moment, then scratched his head. “You could call it boredom, I suppose. I’ve repeated four years. I don’t even know what classes to take anymore. Usually I never leave the dorm, just go online and update the news. I have to talk to somebody, don’t I? So I’m lending you a helping hand!”
“Is that a kind of loneliness too?”
“How did this suddenly become such a lofty question…” Fingel thought. “Probably.”

“What really happens when someone’s lonely? Do they die?” Lu Mingfei asked. “Lonely or not, don’t you still eat and sleep every day? Play if there’s something to play. Stare into space if there isn’t. That passes the time too.”

“That melancholy look makes you seem like a philosopher. But I don’t really understand why you’re suddenly interested in a grand subject like loneliness.” Fingel reached down to feel Lu Mingfei’s forehead. “Fever?”
“No.”
“Lovesick?”

“No. I just think everyone else is so strange. We’re going off to slay dragons, and everyone’s all fired up. I don’t feel a thing. What does slaying dragons have to do with me?” Lu Mingfei lay on his pillow, staring up at the bunk above. “I’m really just an unrelated passerby. Your college is like an anime. I was just a viewer: Code Geass on Monday, Gundam on Tuesday, Bleach on Wednesday, Gintama on Thursday, Dragon Raja on Friday. Then one Friday, whoosh, I got dragged inside, just in time for the climax. When other heroes go slay dragons, some boss shows them the ropes for a few rounds first. Me, I show up and we launch straight into a grand killing spree. Before I even figure out what’s happening, I have to throw away my life over something that has nothing to do with me.”
He sighed and tossed something up to the top bunk. “Here.”
“Hey. What’s this supposed to mean?” Fingel caught it and paused.
It was Lu Mingfei’s student ID.

“It’s my student ID, the one I can use as a credit card. If you hear I’ve died in China, hurry and buy things with it before it gets canceled. A dead man’s credit rating doesn’t matter, right? If he doesn’t pay it back, he doesn’t pay it back,” Lu Mingfei said.
“You really think you’re going to die?”
“I really do.” Lu Mingfei’s gaze was unfocused.
“Then you’re still going?”
“I have a little reason,” Lu Mingfei said. “Forget it. It’s a pointless reason. I won’t tell you.”

“I’m not interested in your reason. But if you really think you’re going to die, we might as well start swiping that card right now! We can call and order two servings of cream of chicken and mushroom soup, with medium filet mignon, foie gras and sablefish rolls for dessert, and a double order of Camus cognac! Your credit limit is a hundred thousand dollars. If we don’t max it out, we’ll never get another chance!” Waving the student ID, Fingel leaped from the top bunk and lunged for the phone.
“Hey!” Lu Mingfei jumped out of bed and grabbed him. “Senior, you’ve got it wrong. Those aren’t your lines! You’re supposed to be moved, then give me some encouragement!”
“I’ll encourage you after I’ve eaten!” With a solemn expression, Fingel held the card high overhead, like a worker holding a book of quotations on a Cultural Revolution propaganda poster.
Lu Mingfei jumped to reach the card. At times like this, Fingel, who habitually hunched, suddenly revealed his full height. Lu Mingfei was like a monkey reaching for a banana.
“I said swipe it after I’m dead, before the card dies too!” Once again, Lu Mingfei experienced the devastating consequences of trusting the wrong person.

“By then it’ll be too late! A hundred thousand dollars. What can you buy at this college? I don’t need designer sports cars. Just a few late-night snacks. Even the fanciest snacks would take hundreds of meals to max this thing out!” Fingel said.

“But I might not die! Maybe I’ll get lucky and survive, come back, look at the bill, and—holy shit—a hundred thousand in credit card debt! Then I’ll have to jump off a building anyway!” Lu Mingfei was frantic. “Damn it, I haven’t heard a thing about a big bonus for this life-threatening operation!”
“You just said you really thought you’d die!”
“That was pessimism! What if I don’t? What if, what if!” Lu Mingfei’s face flushed crimson. That card really was his life. A penniless wretch, he depended on it to get by at this college.
Fingel smacked him on the forehead. His hand was rough, broad, and powerful. The slap left Lu Mingfei stunned.

“Exactly. Now you’ve got it.” Fingel tucked the card back into Lu Mingfei’s pocket, patted his chest, and turned to climb into the top bunk. “There’s always a what-if. Sometimes losers survive too, because losers always have especially good dumb luck. Understand?” He burrowed under his blanket and propped himself against the headboard, working on his laptop. The screen’s blue light illuminated his scruffy face.
Lu Mingfei stared for a long time. “Hey. Is this you encouraging me?”
“We losers have to encourage each other.” Fingel didn’t even look at him.
